mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in UNRATE for three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.4pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in industrial production, reflecting weakening manufacturing activity and reduced corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST of more than 1% and 2% respectively signals a broad-based drop in housing and overall demand, which depresses consumer spending and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < -1% and HOUST < -2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in FEDFUNDS of more than 0.75 percentage points, coinciding with a rise in CPIAUCSL of more than 0.4% in the same month, signals aggressive tightening amid rising inflation, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > +0.75pp AND CPIAUCSL > +0.4% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS of more than 2% for three consecutive months signals a surge in consumer savings, which typically precedes a reduction in consumption and weaker retail sales, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
